subject: problem installing rJava on cluster started by spark-ec2

messages.author: d78486bfff620d81
messages.subject: problem installing rJava on cluster started by spark-ec2
parts:
So I was using SparkR a few weeks ago on EC2 and things were fine. I was starting up a cluster via the spark-ec2 script in Spark 1.1.0 and then I was installing SparkR as follows after logging onto the master node:

cd /root
wget http://cran.cnr.berkeley.edu/src/contrib/rJava_0.9-6.tar.gz
/root/spark-ec2/copy-dir rJava_0.9-6.tar.gz
R CMD javareconf
tar xvzf rJava_0.9-6.tar.gz; R CMD INSTALL rJava
/root/spark/sbin/slaves.sh R CMD javareconf; R CMD INSTALL ~/rJava_0.9-6.tar.gz

cd /root
git clone https://github.com/amplab-extras/SparkR-pkg.git
cd SparkR-pkg
./install-dev.sh
/root/spark-ec2/copy-dir /root/SparkR-pkg


Now when I try to do the R CMD javareconf step, I'm having an issue with setting the path to libjvm.so (see log info  below). I can muck around with environment variables but thought I'd see if anyone else had had this problem before I hacked together my own fix. This issue is happening either if I start the EC2 cluster using spark-ec2 from Spark 1.1.0 or Spark 1.1.1. It's particularly odd that this happens when I use Spark 1.1.0 as I don't see what would have changed relative to a few weeks ago...

messages.author: f4108b5f63668d70
messages.subject: Re: problem installing rJava on cluster started by spark-ec2
parts: I've run into this before and the problem is the error caused by the following lines

/usr/lib64/R/bin/javareconf: line 250: /usr/bin/realpath: No such file or directory
/bin/sed: -e expression #1, char 0: no previous regular expression

I found a workaround at http://superuser.com/questions/771104/usr-bin-realpath-not-found-in-centos-6-5 which suggests using readlink -e instead of realpath.
I think I just edited javareconf to fix things, but you could also create an alias or make a simple bash script named realpath which just calls readlink -e

Let me know if this works for you and I can try and add this fix to the Spark EC2 setup scripts

Thanks
Shivaram

Hi Shivaram, thanks.

Yes, creating a bash script for /usr/bin/realpath worked for me. If
you guys could either post instructions for that on the SparkR webpage
(where you currently make a note about running R CMD javareconf) or
even better modify spark-ec2, that would be very helpful.

More generally, it would also be helpful if you all posted the full
set of commands a user on EC2 would need to install SparkR on the
SparkR webpage, including how to install rJava, and how to make sure
things are set up on both master and workers.

chris
